name: The Greek Miracle: Cities, Gods and Ideas
description: How a scatter of small cities around the Aegean produced democracy, drama, history, geometry and philosophy, and then spread them from Egypt to India.

checkpoints.name: Palaces and heroes
checkpoints.note: On Crete and the mainland, palace kingdoms kept records in Linear B after a giant eruption shook the Aegean. Later poets sang of a great war at Troy, and the Trojan War became the main story of Greece.

checkpoints.name: Poets, games and city-states
checkpoints.note: The Greeks borrowed an alphabet, and Homer's Iliad and Odyssey were set down. Cities met at the Olympic Games and the oracle at Delphi, honoured their gods, and produced Sappho the poet and Thales the first scientist.

checkpoints.name: War with Persia and the golden age
checkpoints.note: Athens and Sparta turned back the Persians at Marathon, Thermopylae and Salamis. Under Pericles, Athens built the Parthenon and staged tragedies like Antigone, until the Peloponnesian War and a plague shattered it.

checkpoints.name: Thinkers and a conqueror
checkpoints.note: After the trial of Socrates his pupil Plato taught, and Aristotle taught Alexander the Great. Alexander then conquered an empire stretching to India and spread Greek language far from home.

checkpoints.name: The Hellenistic world
checkpoints.note: Greek culture ruled the successor kingdoms. Euclid and Archimedes advanced mathematics, Stoicism taught calm, and artists made the Colossus of Rhodes and the Venus de Milo before Rome absorbed it all.
